<tr><td>

[fetchAccrualVaultV2(address, client, parameters)](#blue-sdk-viem.fetchaccrualvaultv2)


</td><td>

Fetches VaultV2 state with accrual data for capacity calculations.

Reads all state fetched by `fetchVaultV2`<!-- -->, the vault asset balance, accrual state for the configured liquidity adapter and regular adapters, and force-deallocate penalties. By default it reads the entire tree in a single deployless call and only falls back to sequential multicall reads when that call fails; pass `deployless: "force"` to require the single call, or `deployless: false` to use multicall reads directly.

`MorphoMarketV1Adapter` has zero support as a VaultV2 liquidity adapter. This fetcher may hydrate that adapter as an accrual adapter, but liquidity cap allocations remain undefined because `fetchVaultV2` only loads allocations for `MorphoVaultV1Adapter` and `MorphoMarketV1AdapterV2`<!-- -->. Calling `maxDeposit` on the returned `AccrualVaultV2` therefore throws `VaultV2Errors.UnsupportedLiquidityAdapter` for a non-V2 market adapter liquidity adapter.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[fetchAccrualVaultV2Adapter(address, client, parameters)](#blue-sdk-viem.fetchaccrualvaultv2adapter)


</td><td>

Fetches a VaultV2 adapter with the accrued state required for allocation calculations.

Reads the configured adapter factories, then delegates to the matching accrual adapter fetcher.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[fetchAccrualVaultV2Deployless(address, client, parameters)](#blue-sdk-viem.fetchaccrualvaultv2deployless)


</td><td>

Fetches the full VaultV2 accrual tree in a single deployless call.

[fetchAccrualVaultV2()](#blue-sdk-viem.fetchaccrualvaultv2) defaults to this same single deployless call but transparently falls back to sequential multicall reads (vault, then each adapter, then each adapter's markets or wrapped MetaMorpho V1 vault) when the deployless read fails. This reader is deployless-only: it always performs the single `eth_call`<!-- -->, never falls back, and throws if the deployless read fails (equivalent to `deployless: "force"`<!-- -->). It requires every configured adapter factory to be deployed at the queried block.

The returned `AccrualVaultV2` is byte-for-byte identical to `fetchAccrualVaultV2`<!-- -->'s output, including the nested MetaMorpho V1 vault of a `MorphoVaultV1Adapter`<!-- -->: its EIP-5267 domain (`eip5267Domain`<!-- -->) and PublicAllocator config (both vault-level and per-market `publicAllocatorConfig`<!-- -->) are read in the same single call, so no field is dropped.


</td></tr>

[fetchVaultV2(address, client, parameters)](#blue-sdk-viem.fetchvaultv2)


</td><td>

Fetches VaultV2 state and liquidity-cap data.

Reads token metadata, vault accounting, fee configuration and recipient share eligibility, adapter addresses, the configured liquidity adapter, liquidity data, and cap allocations for supported liquidity adapters. Uses the deployless `GetVaultV2` query by default and falls back to multicall when allowed.

`MorphoMarketV1Adapter` has zero support as a VaultV2 liquidity adapter. This fetcher only loads liquidity allocations for `MorphoVaultV1Adapter` and `MorphoMarketV1AdapterV2`<!-- -->; when a vault configures the non-V2 market adapter as `liquidityAdapter`<!-- -->, the returned `VaultV2` preserves the adapter address and liquidity data but leaves `liquidityAllocations` undefined. Fetch `MorphoMarketV1Adapter` through `fetchVaultV2Adapter` when it is used as a regular adapter.


</td></tr>

<tr><td>

[readContractRestructured(client, parameters)](#blue-sdk-viem.readcontractrestructured)


</td><td>

When reading contracts, viem converts onchain tuples into arrays -- even when tuple values are named in the ABI. \[They argue\](https://viem.sh/docs/faq\#why-is-a-contract-function-return-type-returning-an-array-instead-of-an-object) this information loss is justified, as it eliminates the ambiguity between tuple return types and struct return types. This wrapper converts viem's arrays back to objects, \_as if\_ the onchain method returned a struct.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[restructure(outputs, parameters)](#blue-sdk-viem.restructure)


</td><td>

When reading contracts, viem converts onchain tuples into arrays -- even when tuple values are named in the ABI. \[They argue\](https://viem.sh/docs/faq\#why-is-a-contract-function-return-type-returning-an-array-instead-of-an-object) this information loss is justified, as it eliminates the ambiguity between tuple return types and struct return types. This utility can be used to convert viem's arrays back to objects, \_as if\_ the onchain method returned a struct.


</td></tr>

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.fetchaccrualposition"></a>

## fetchAccrualPosition() function

Fetches a user's Morpho Blue position with accrued market state.

Reads the raw user position and the current market state, then combines them into an `AccrualPosition`<!-- -->.

- `parameters.blockTag`<!-- -->: Optional block tag for historical reads.

- `parameters.stateOverride`<!-- -->: Optional viem state override.

- `parameters.chainId`<!-- -->: Optional chain id; defaults to `getChainId(client)`<!-- -->.

```ts
import type { AccrualPosition, MarketId } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk";
import { fetchAccrualPosition } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";
```

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.fetchaccrualvaultv2"></a>

## fetchAccrualVaultV2() function

Fetches VaultV2 state with accrual data for capacity calculations.

Reads all state fetched by `fetchVaultV2`<!-- -->, the vault asset balance, accrual state for the configured liquidity adapter and regular adapters, and force-deallocate penalties. By default it reads the entire tree in a single deployless call and only falls back to sequential multicall reads when that call fails; pass `deployless: "force"` to require the single call, or `deployless: false` to use multicall reads directly.

`MorphoMarketV1Adapter` has zero support as a VaultV2 liquidity adapter. This fetcher may hydrate that adapter as an accrual adapter, but liquidity cap allocations remain undefined because `fetchVaultV2` only loads allocations for `MorphoVaultV1Adapter` and `MorphoMarketV1AdapterV2`<!-- -->. Calling `maxDeposit` on the returned `AccrualVaultV2` therefore throws `VaultV2Errors.UnsupportedLiquidityAdapter` for a non-V2 market adapter liquidity adapter.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function fetchAccrualVaultV2(address: Address, client: Client, parameters?: DeploylessFetchParameters): Promise<AccrualVaultV2>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

address


</td><td>

Address


</td><td>

Address of the VaultV2 to fetch.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

client


</td><td>

Client


</td><td>

Viem client used for deployless reads or multicalls.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

parameters


</td><td>

[DeploylessFetchParameters](#blue-sdk-viem.deploylessfetchparameters)


</td><td>

_(Optional)_


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;[AccrualVaultV2](./blue-sdk.md#blue-sdk.accrualvaultv2)<!-- -->&gt;

The hydrated `AccrualVaultV2` entity with asset balance, accrual adapters, and force-deallocate penalties.

## Exceptions

`UnknownFactory` when the configured chain has no VaultV2 factory.

`UnknownOfFactory` when `address` is not a VaultV2 from the configured factory.

`UnsupportedVaultV2AdapterError` when the vault or one of its adapters uses an unsupported adapter class.

`viem.BaseError` when a read fails with no fallback left (`deployless: "force"`<!-- -->, or a multicall read when `deployless: false`<!-- -->).

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `parameters.account`<!-- -->: Optional account passed to viem calls.

- `parameters.blockNumber`<!-- -->: Optional block number for historical reads.

- `parameters.blockTag`<!-- -->: Optional block tag for historical reads.

- `parameters.stateOverride`<!-- -->: Optional viem state override.

- `parameters.chainId`<!-- -->: Optional chain id; defaults to `getChainId(client)`<!-- -->.

- `parameters.deployless`<!-- -->: Optional deployless read mode; defaults to `true`<!-- -->.

## Example


```ts
import type { AccrualVaultV2 } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk";
import { fetchAccrualVaultV2 } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";
import { createPublicClient, http } from "viem";
import { base } from "viem/chains";

const client = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http() });
const vaultV2Address = "0xfDE48B9B8568189f629Bc5209bf5FA826336557a";

const vault: AccrualVaultV2 = await fetchAccrualVaultV2(vaultV2Address, client);
```

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.fetchaccrualvaultv2deployless"></a>

## fetchAccrualVaultV2Deployless() function

> Warning: This API is now obsolete.
>
> Use [fetchAccrualVaultV2()](#blue-sdk-viem.fetchaccrualvaultv2)<!-- -->, which is deployless-first with RPC fallback by default. Pass `deployless: "force"` to preserve this function's no-fallback behavior.
>

Fetches the full VaultV2 accrual tree in a single deployless call.

[fetchAccrualVaultV2()](#blue-sdk-viem.fetchaccrualvaultv2) defaults to this same single deployless call but transparently falls back to sequential multicall reads (vault, then each adapter, then each adapter's markets or wrapped MetaMorpho V1 vault) when the deployless read fails. This reader is deployless-only: it always performs the single `eth_call`<!-- -->, never falls back, and throws if the deployless read fails (equivalent to `deployless: "force"`<!-- -->). It requires every configured adapter factory to be deployed at the queried block.

The returned `AccrualVaultV2` is byte-for-byte identical to `fetchAccrualVaultV2`<!-- -->'s output, including the nested MetaMorpho V1 vault of a `MorphoVaultV1Adapter`<!-- -->: its EIP-5267 domain (`eip5267Domain`<!-- -->) and PublicAllocator config (both vault-level and per-market `publicAllocatorConfig`<!-- -->) are read in the same single call, so no field is dropped.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function fetchAccrualVaultV2Deployless(address: Address, client: Client, parameters?: FetchParameters): Promise<AccrualVaultV2>;
```

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

address


</td><td>

Address


</td><td>

Address of the VaultV2 to fetch.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

client


</td><td>

parameters

Promise&lt;[AccrualVaultV2](./blue-sdk.md#blue-sdk.accrualvaultv2)<!-- -->&gt;

The hydrated `AccrualVaultV2` entity with asset balance, accrued liquidity and regular adapters, and force-deallocate penalties.

## Exceptions

`UnknownFactory` when the configured chain has no VaultV2 factory.

`UnknownOfFactory` when `address` is not a VaultV2 from the configured factory.

`UnsupportedVaultV2AdapterError` when the vault or one of its adapters uses an unsupported adapter class.

`viem.BaseError` when the deployless `eth_call` or response decoding fails (no fallback).

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `parameters.account`<!-- -->: Optional account passed to the viem call.

- `parameters.blockNumber`<!-- -->: Optional block number for a historical read.

- `parameters.blockTag`<!-- -->: Optional block tag for a historical read.

- `parameters.stateOverride`<!-- -->: Optional viem state override.

- `parameters.chainId`<!-- -->: Optional chain id; defaults to `getChainId(client)`<!-- -->.

## Example


```ts
import type { AccrualVaultV2 } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk";
import { fetchAccrualVaultV2Deployless } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";
import { createPublicClient, http } from "viem";
import { base } from "viem/chains";

const client = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http() });
const vaultV2Address = "0xfDE48B9B8568189f629Bc5209bf5FA826336557a";

const vault: AccrualVaultV2 = await fetchAccrualVaultV2Deployless(
  vaultV2Address,
  client,
);
```

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.fetchvaultv2"></a>

## fetchVaultV2() function

Fetches VaultV2 state and liquidity-cap data.

Reads token metadata, vault accounting, fee configuration and recipient share eligibility, adapter addresses, the configured liquidity adapter, liquidity data, and cap allocations for supported liquidity adapters. Uses the deployless `GetVaultV2` query by default and falls back to multicall when allowed.

`MorphoMarketV1Adapter` has zero support as a VaultV2 liquidity adapter. This fetcher only loads liquidity allocations for `MorphoVaultV1Adapter` and `MorphoMarketV1AdapterV2`<!-- -->; when a vault configures the non-V2 market adapter as `liquidityAdapter`<!-- -->, the returned `VaultV2` preserves the adapter address and liquidity data but leaves `liquidityAllocations` undefined. Fetch `MorphoMarketV1Adapter` through `fetchVaultV2Adapter` when it is used as a regular adapter.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function fetchVaultV2(address: Address, client: Client, parameters?: DeploylessFetchParameters): Promise<VaultV2>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

address


</td><td>

Address


</td><td>

Address of the VaultV2 to fetch.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

client


</td><td>

Client


</td><td>

Viem client used for deployless reads or multicalls.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

parameters


</td><td>

[DeploylessFetchParameters](#blue-sdk-viem.deploylessfetchparameters)


</td><td>

_(Optional)_


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;[VaultV2](./blue-sdk.md#blue-sdk.vaultv2)<!-- -->&gt;

The hydrated `VaultV2` entity. `liquidityAllocations` is undefined when no liquidity adapter is configured or when the configured liquidity adapter is unsupported.

## Exceptions

`UnknownFactory` when the configured chain has no VaultV2 factory.

`UnknownOfFactory` when `address` is not a VaultV2 from the configured factory.

`UnsupportedVaultV2AdapterError` when a recognized liquidity adapter is configured with unsupported liquidity data.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `parameters.account`<!-- -->: Optional account passed to viem calls.

- `parameters.blockNumber`<!-- -->: Optional block number for historical reads.

- `parameters.blockTag`<!-- -->: Optional block tag for historical reads.

- `parameters.stateOverride`<!-- -->: Optional viem state override.

- `parameters.chainId`<!-- -->: Optional chain id; defaults to `getChainId(client)`<!-- -->.

- `parameters.deployless`<!-- -->: Optional deployless read mode; defaults to `true`<!-- -->.

## Example


```ts
import type { VaultV2 } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk";
import { fetchVaultV2 } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";
import { createPublicClient, http } from "viem";
import { base } from "viem/chains";

const client = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http() });
const vaultV2Address = "0xfDE48B9B8568189f629Bc5209bf5FA826336557a";

const vault: VaultV2 = await fetchVaultV2(vaultV2Address, client);
```

```ts
import { type Address, createPublicClient, type Hash, http } from "viem";
import { mainnet } from "viem/chains";

const client = createPublicClient({ chain: mainnet, transport: http() });
export async function fetchMarketAllocatorConfig(
  vault: Address,
  adapter: Address,
  adapterMarketCapId: Hash,
): Promise<VaultV2BlueMarketPublicAllocatorConfig> {
  return fetchVaultV2BlueMarketPublicAllocatorConfig(
    vault,
    adapter,
    adapterMarketCapId,
    client,
  );
}
```

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.fetchvaultv2bluepublicallocatordata"></a>

## fetchVaultV2BluePublicAllocatorData() function

Fetches all BluePublicAllocator and Vault V2 cap data needed to simulate reallocations for one hydrated Vault V2.

Only `VaultV2MorphoMarketV1AdapterV2` adapters participate. The function derives every adapter-market id and shared vault allocation id from the hydrated vault, uses one deployless `eth_call` by default, and falls back to direct reads unless deployless mode is forced.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function fetchVaultV2BluePublicAllocatorData(vault: AccrualVaultV2, client: Client, parameters?: DeploylessFetchParameters & {
    readonly targetMarketParams?: MarketParams;
}): Promise<{
    publicAllocatorConfig: VaultV2BluePublicAllocatorConfig | undefined;
    activeAdapters: Set<`0x${string}`>;
    marketPublicAllocatorConfigs: Record<`0x${string}`, VaultV2BlueMarketPublicAllocatorConfig | undefined>;
    allocations: Record<`0x${string}`, IVaultV2Allocation | undefined>;
}>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

vault


</td><td>

[AccrualVaultV2](./blue-sdk.md#blue-sdk.accrualvaultv2)


</td><td>

Hydrated Vault V2 whose accrued adapters provide the candidate markets.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

client


</td><td>

Client


</td><td>

Viem client used for deployless or direct reads.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

parameters


</td><td>

[DeploylessFetchParameters](#blue-sdk-viem.deploylessfetchparameters) &amp; { readonly targetMarketParams?: [MarketParams](./blue-sdk.md#blue-sdk.marketparams)<!-- -->; }


</td><td>

_(Optional)_


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;{ publicAllocatorConfig: [VaultV2BluePublicAllocatorConfig](./blue-sdk.md#blue-sdk.vaultv2bluepublicallocatorconfig) \| undefined; activeAdapters: Set&lt;\`0x${string}\`&gt;; marketPublicAllocatorConfigs: Record&lt;\`0x${string}\`, [VaultV2BlueMarketPublicAllocatorConfig](./blue-sdk.md#blue-sdk.vaultv2bluemarketpublicallocatorconfig) \| undefined&gt;; allocations: Record&lt;\`0x${string}\`, [IVaultV2Allocation](./blue-sdk.md#blue-sdk.ivaultv2allocation) \| undefined&gt;; }&gt;

Vault-wide config when the BluePublicAllocator is authorized, active-adapter set, adapter-market configs keyed by `adapterMarketCapId`<!-- -->, and allocations keyed by derived id.

## Exceptions

`UnknownAddressError` when the chain has no BluePublicAllocator deployment.

`UnsupportedChainIdError` when the chain is absent from the address registry.

`viem.BaseError` when deployless mode is forced and fails, or when a direct contract read fails.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `parameters.account`<!-- -->: Optional account passed to viem calls.

- `parameters.blockNumber`<!-- -->: Optional block number for historical reads.

- `parameters.blockTag`<!-- -->: Optional block tag for historical reads.

- `parameters.stateOverride`<!-- -->: Optional viem state override.

- `parameters.chainId`<!-- -->: Optional chain id; defaults to `getChainId(client)`<!-- -->.

- `parameters.deployless`<!-- -->: Deployless mode; defaults to `true`<!-- -->, with direct-read fallback.

- `parameters.targetMarketParams`<!-- -->: Optional target market whose config and cap ids are fetched even when the adapter has no current position.

## Example


```ts
import type { AccrualVaultV2 } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk";
import { fetchVaultV2BluePublicAllocatorData } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";
import { createPublicClient, http } from "viem";
import { mainnet } from "viem/chains";

const client = createPublicClient({ chain: mainnet, transport: http() });
export async function fetchAllocatorData(
  vault: AccrualVaultV2,
) {
  const data = await fetchVaultV2BluePublicAllocatorData(vault, client);
  // data contains publicAllocatorConfig, activeAdapters, marketPublicAllocatorConfigs, and allocations.
  return data;
}
```

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.getdaipermittypeddata"></a>

## getDaiPermitTypedData() function

> Warning: This API is now obsolete.
>
> Not used by any SDK flow — DAI approvals are routed through Permit2 / classic approval internally (DAI's non-standard permit is incompatible with the ERC-2612 simple-permit path). Prefer the Permit2 flow. Scheduled for removal in the next major.
>

Builds DAI-style permit typed data for signing.

**Signature:**

```typescript
getDaiPermitTypedData: (args: DaiPermitArgs, chainId: ChainId) => TypedDataDefinition<typeof daiPermitTypes, "Permit">
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

args


</td><td>

[DaiPermitArgs](#blue-sdk-viem.daipermitargs)


</td><td>

DAI permit message fields.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

chainId


</td><td>

[ChainId](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.chainid)


</td><td>

Chain id whose DAI deployment verifies the signature.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

TypedDataDefinition&lt;typeof daiPermitTypes, "Permit"&gt;

Typed data ready to pass to a wallet for signing.

## Remarks

DAI's permit is \*\*boolean\*\*: any `allowance > 0n` authorizes the spender for `type(uint256).max`<!-- -->, not the passed amount — there is no finite-allowance DAI permit.

## Example


```ts
import { ChainId } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk";
import { getDaiPermitTypedData } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";

const typedData = getDaiPermitTypedData(
  {
    owner: "0xBBBBBbbBBb9cC5e90e3b3Af64bdAF62C37EEFFCb",
    spender: "0x6566194141fF46b819c55E7137D8329898eCd06C",
    allowance: 1_000_000_000_000_000_000n,
    nonce: 0n,
    deadline: 1_900_000_000n,
  },
  ChainId.EthMainnet,
);
```

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.getpermittypeddata"></a>

## getPermitTypedData() function

Permit signature for ERC20 tokens, following EIP-2612. Fails closed when fetched EIP-5267 metadata is not bound to the token and chain. Consumers should use another approval path instead of signing an unsafe domain. Docs: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612

**Signature:**

```typescript
getPermitTypedData: (args: PermitArgs, chainId: ChainId) => TypedDataDefinition<typeof permitTypes, "Permit">
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

args


</td><td>

[PermitArgs](#blue-sdk-viem.permitargs)


</td><td>

The permit message fields and ERC20 token metadata.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

chainId


</td><td>

[ChainId](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.chainid)


</td><td>

The expected chain ID for the permit domain.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

TypedDataDefinition&lt;typeof permitTypes, "Permit"&gt;

Typed data ready to pass to a wallet for signing.

## Exceptions

InvalidPermitDomainChainIdError when fetched EIP-5267 metadata targets another chain or omits `chainId`<!-- -->.

InvalidPermitDomainVerifyingContractError when fetched EIP-5267 metadata targets another token or omits `verifyingContract`<!-- -->.

UnsupportedPermitDomainExtensionsError when fetched EIP-5267 metadata advertises extension fields unsupported by this helper.

## Example

import { getPermitTypedData } from "<!-- -->@<!-- -->morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";

const typedData = getPermitTypedData( { erc20: token, owner, spender, allowance: 1\_000000n, nonce, deadline, }<!-- -->, ChainId.EthMainnet, ); const signature = await walletClient.signTypedData(typedData);

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.getunsupportedvaultv2adapter"></a>

## getUnsupportedVaultV2Adapter() function

Checks if an error is a contract revert with the "UnsupportedVaultV2Adapter" error name, returning the offending adapter address if so. Used to propagate adapter validation errors from the deployless `GetVaultV2.query` to the caller as a typed .

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function getUnsupportedVaultV2Adapter(error: unknown): Address | null;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

error


</td><td>

unknown


</td><td>

Error thrown by viem or another read path.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

[Address](./blue-sdk.md#blue-sdk.address) \| null

The unsupported adapter address when present, or `null` when the error does not match.

## Example


```ts
import { UnsupportedVaultV2AdapterError } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk";
import { getUnsupportedVaultV2Adapter } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";

const adapter = getUnsupportedVaultV2Adapter(error);
if (adapter != null) throw new UnsupportedVaultV2AdapterError(adapter);
```

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.isunknownoffactoryerror"></a>

## isUnknownOfFactoryError() function

Checks if an error is a contract revert with the "UnknownOfFactory" error name.

Used to propagate factory validation errors instead of falling back to multicall.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function isUnknownOfFactoryError(error: unknown): boolean;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

error


</td><td>

unknown


</td><td>

Error thrown by viem or another read path.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

boolean

`true` when `error` wraps a viem `ContractFunctionRevertedError` named `UnknownOfFactory`<!-- -->.

## Example


```ts
import { isUnknownOfFactoryError } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";

if (isUnknownOfFactoryError(error)) throw error;
```

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.metamorphoaction.acceptcap"></a>

## MetaMorphoAction.acceptCap() function

Encodes a call to a MetaMorpho vault to accept the pending supply cap.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function acceptCap(marketParams: InputMarketParams): MetaMorphoCall;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

marketParams


</td><td>

[InputMarketParams](./blue-sdk.md#blue-sdk.inputmarketparams)


</td><td>

The market params of the market of which to accept the pending supply cap.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

[MetaMorphoCall](#blue-sdk-viem.metamorphocall)

ABI-encoded MetaMorpho calldata as a `MetaMorphoCall`<!-- -->.

## Example


```ts
import type { InputMarketParams } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";
import { MetaMorphoAction } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";

const marketParams = {
  loanToken: "0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48",
  collateralToken: "0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2",
  oracle: zeroAddress,
  irm: "0x870aC11D48B15DB9a138Cf899d20F13F79Ba00BC",
  lltv: 860_000_000_000_000_000n,
} satisfies InputMarketParams;

const call = MetaMorphoAction.acceptCap(marketParams);
```

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.readcontractrestructured"></a>

## readContractRestructured() function

When reading contracts, viem converts onchain tuples into arrays -- even when tuple values are named in the ABI. \[They argue\](https://viem.sh/docs/faq\#why-is-a-contract-function-return-type-returning-an-array-instead-of-an-object) this information loss is justified, as it eliminates the ambiguity between tuple return types and struct return types. This wrapper converts viem's arrays back to objects, \_as if\_ the onchain method returned a struct.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function readContractRestructured<chain extends Chain | undefined, const abi extends Abi, name extends AbiItemName<abi> & ContractFunctionName<abi, "view" | "pure">, const args extends ContractFunctionArgs<abi, "view" | "pure", name>>(client: Client<Transport, chain>, parameters: ReadContractParameters<abi, name, args>): Promise<ZipToObject<ExtractAbiFunctionForArgs<abi, "pure" | "view", name, args>["outputs"], Awaited<import("viem").ContractFunctionReturnType<abi, "pure" | "view", name, args>> extends infer T ? T extends Awaited<import("viem").ContractFunctionReturnType<abi, "pure" | "view", name, args>> ? T extends readonly unknown[] ? T : never : never : never>>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

client


</td><td>

Client&lt;Transport, chain&gt;


</td><td>

Viem client used for the read.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

parameters


</td><td>

ReadContractParameters&lt;abi, name, args&gt;


</td><td>

Read contract parameters for a view or pure function with named tuple outputs.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;ZipToObject&lt;ExtractAbiFunctionForArgs&lt;abi, "pure" \| "view", name, args&gt;\["outputs"\], Awaited&lt;import("viem").ContractFunctionReturnType&lt;abi, "pure" \| "view", name, args&gt;&gt; extends infer T ? T extends Awaited&lt;import("viem").ContractFunctionReturnType&lt;abi, "pure" \| "view", name, args&gt;&gt; ? T extends readonly unknown\[\] ? T : never : never : never&gt;&gt;

An object whose keys are the named ABI outputs and whose values are the tuple elements.

## Example


```ts
import { readContractRestructured } from "@morpho-org/blue-sdk-viem";

const market = await readContractRestructured(client, {
  address: morpho,
  abi: blueAbi,
  functionName: "market",
  args: [marketId],
});
```

<a name="blue-sdk-viem.restructure"></a>

## restructure() function

When reading contracts, viem converts onchain tuples into arrays -- even when tuple values are named in the ABI. \[They argue\](https://viem.sh/docs/faq\#why-is-a-contract-function-return-type-returning-an-array-instead-of-an-object) this information loss is justified, as it eliminates the ambiguity between tuple return types and struct return types. This utility can be used to convert viem's arrays back to objects, \_as if\_ the onchain method returned a struct.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function restructure<const abi extends Abi, name extends AbiItemName<abi> & ContractFunctionName<abi, "view" | "pure">, const args extends AbiItemArgs<abi, name>, outputs extends readonly unknown[]>(outputs: outputs, parameters: GetAbiItemParameters<abi, name, args>): ZipToObject<ExtractAbiFunctionForArgs<abi, "pure" | "view", name, args>["outputs"], outputs>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

outputs


</td><td>

outputs


</td><td>

Tuple output returned by viem.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

parameters


</td><td>

GetAbiItemParameters&lt;abi, name, args&gt;


</td><td>

ABI item lookup parameters matching the read that produced `outputs`<!-- -->.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

ZipToObject&lt;ExtractAbiFunctionForArgs&lt;abi, "pure" \| "view", name, args&gt;\["outputs"\], outputs&gt;

An object whose keys are the named ABI outputs and whose values are the tuple elements.

## Example 1


```
// Use with viem...
const params = restructure(
  await readContract(client, {
    ...parameters,
    address: morpho,
    abi: blueAbi,
    functionName: "idToMarketParams",
    args: [id],
  }),
  // These `args` should be placeholders; just match the type of the actual `args` above
  { abi: blueAbi, name: "idToMarketParams", args: ["0x"] },
)
```

## Example 2


```
// Use with wagmi hook...
const { data: marketsData } = useReadContracts({
  contracts: marketIds.map(
    (marketId) =>
      ({
        chainId,
        address: morphoAddress,
        abi: morphoAbi,
        functionName: "market",
        args: [marketId],
      }) as const,
  ),
  allowFailure: false,
  query: {
    select(data) {
      // These `args` should be placeholders; just match the type of the actual `args` above
      return data.map((x) => restructure(x, { abi: morphoAbi, name: "market", args: ["0x"] }));
    },
  },
});
```
